From Python (psa) to SLA > Functions and Tuples

Functions and Tuples

Function Definitions and Return

psa's def needs no type annotations (the census records parameter/return annotations as not supported), and it supports default values, keyword arguments, and *args/**kwargs. SLA's fn is fully typed — every parameter and the return type are written — and has no default values: callers pass every argument, explicitly. Both sides return with return.

psaSLA
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

def divmod(a, b):
    return (a // b, a % b)

print(add(10, 20))   # 30
q, r = divmod(17, 5)
print(f"{q},{r}")    # 3,2
 
@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"

fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    return a + b;
}

fn divmod(a: i32, b: i32) -> (i32, i32) {
    return (a / b, a % b);
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    println("{}", add(10, 20));
    let (q, r) = divmod(17, 5);
    println("{},{}", q, r);
    return 0;
}

Verified output (SLA): 30, 3,2, exit code 0. Note that the returned tuple here is built from computed values; literal tuples are the next topic.

Tuples

Both sides have tuples and destructuring: psa unpacks by assignment, SLA by let (a, b) = ..., and SLA tuple fields are read as t.0, t.1 (psa indexes t[0], t[1]). The census marks psa tuple literals and unpacking as supported.

One measured SLA defect, recorded rather than hidden: a tuple literal written into an (i32, i32) position misreads its second element on the verified toolchain (the literal is stored at 8-byte stride while the projection reads at 4-byte stride; the corpus registers this as DEF-TEXT-TUPLE-PROJ-SUBWORD-OFFSET, with a regression test in the plugin's test corpus). The (i64, i64) form below is the verified-correct spelling and is what this section uses.

psaSLA
def swap(p):
    return (p[1], p[0])

t = (3, 8)
print(f"{t[0]},{t[1]}")  # 3,8
s = swap(t)
print(f"{s[0]},{s[1]}")  # 8,3
 
@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"

fn swap(p: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
    return (p.1, p.0);
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    let t: (i64, i64) = (3, 8);
    println("{},{}", t.0, t.1);
    let s = swap(t);
    println("{},{}", s.0, s.1);
    return 0;
}

Verified output (SLA): 3,8, 8,3, exit code 0.

Key Points of This Page

  • def ↔ fn: psa is unannotated and supports defaults/keyword/variable arguments; SLA is fully typed with no defaults.
  • Multiple return values are tuples on both sides; destructuring is assignment in psa, let (a, b) in SLA.
  • Measured defect: (i32, i32) tuple literals misread element 1 on the verified toolchain — use the (i64, i64) form, as shown.
